description: Developing Urban Resilience is a library of short case briefs on real estate projects and city policies that address climate shocks and stresses at site scale, such as sea level rise, storms, heat, drought, wildfire and earthquakes. The Urban Land Institute's Urban Resilience Program maintains it, with themed collections on coastal resilience, resilient parks and open spaces, green infrastructure and city policies, and it invites nominations of new projects. Coverage is mostly United States cities, with projects such as Seattle's Aurora Bioswales, Penn Park in Philadelphia and Meander Bend Park in Tucson. Briefs can be filtered by hazard, project type, policy type, design strategy (green infrastructure, backup power, flood walls, resilience hubs) and value created, including avoided losses and reduced insurance premiums. Format and access: web briefs, free, with the related ULI reports on the members' site. Licence: ULI website terms, not read. Caveats: briefs are written from developer information and are qualitative. It gives analogues for climate adaptation and resilience investment cases. Related catalogue records are the susdrain SuDS case studies and the NYC Green Infrastructure Program.
